messages:
Tyler (CSM): Heads-up — OrchidPay (sales) just asked for a dedicated capacity reservation. They want embeddings + chat serving with a large burst window. Can product scope this as a formal intake?
Elaine (PM): Thanks Tyler. Do we have the numbers? QPS / latency / burst duration?
Tyler (CSM): Notes from the call: target steady-state 200 QPS embeddings reads, 150 QPS chat generates. Peak bursts up to 2k QPS for ~10 minutes, maybe twice a day. Latency target <300ms p95 for embeddings, <400ms p95 for chat.
Maria (Solutions Eng): Quick follow — embeddings model is the smaller footprint, chat uses a 13B with kv-cache. If bursts are 2k, cache warming and batching become critical.
Sam (Infra Eng): Rough ballpark for GPU pools: steady 200 qps embeddings could sit on 2xA100 for embeddings if batched well. Chat steady 150 QPS likely needs ~4xA100 shared with batching + caching. For 2k peak with safe headroom we might need spare burst pool ~6-8 GPUs or autoscale to fleet.
Vedant (SRE): We need to agree on autoscaling policy: cold-start limit, max nodes, cooldown. If we allow a 10-minute burst to 2k, autoscale should pre-warm to avoid exceeding latency SLOs. Can we get a traffic pattern?
Tyler (CSM): They said burst is event-driven (promo emails) and predictable 10–15 min windows. They can give us a signal webhook so we can pre-warm.
Elaine (PM): Launch criteria idea: (1) validated workload profile from customer (2) autoscale policy + pre-warm webhook integration implemented (3) cost estimate + customer commit agreed (4) run capacity smoke test and 1h soak. Thoughts?
Maria (Solutions Eng): Agree. Also we should include model fallback plan — if dedicated is saturated route to hosted cheaper variant (quantized) with warning headers. Customer wants no user-facing errors.
Sam (Infra Eng): For sizing calc, quick math: assume chat request avg tokens 300 -> avg GPU time ~50ms/token? hmm.. let me do quick snippet:
```
# extremely rough
chat_qps = 150
avg_tokens = 300
tokens_per_sec = chat_qps * avg_tokens  # 45k t/s
# if GPU can do ~1M tokens/s (optimized) then 0.045 GPUs -> but that's optimistic
```
Not perfect, but real-world throughput depends on batching and kv-cache.
Vedant (SRE): We shouldn't rely on optimistic kernel numbers for commit. Use observed perf from similar customers: 13B chat at p95 350ms with 1.5k concurrency on 8 GPUs in our tests. I'll pull perf matrix.
Tyler (CSM): Sales asked for a committed price band. They'd sign a 12-month reserved with burst credits. Need a monthly cost delta for Dedicated vs Hosted.
Elaine (PM): Product asks to provide 2 options for the customer and sales: (A) Reserved pool with pre-warm webhook + 8 burst GPUs (SLA 99.9) — higher fixed monthly; (B) Hybrid: smaller reserved + fallback to hosted at higher per-token rate during burst — cheaper but depends on fallback quality. Include rollout plan and MTRs.
Maria (Solutions Eng): I'll draft a recommended config for both options and include pre-warm webhook spec, sample payload, and expected warm-up timelines.
Sam (Infra Eng): FYI: autoscale cooldown default 5m — need to make this configurable per-customer. For 10–15 min bursts we should set cooldown 2m and pre-warm window 3m. Ops will also need a cap to avoid runaway scaling.
Vedant (SRE): Add health checks + graceful degradation policy: return 429s only after fallback exhausted; telemetry hooks so customer can see when fallback used.
Tyler (CSM): Next steps: Elaine to prioritize intake, Maria to produce config + webhook spec, Sam to provide nominal GPU count & ops constraints, Vedant to attach perf matrix. I'll coordinate with sales for commit.
Elaine (PM): I'll put this in the backlog as "orchidpay-dedicated-intake" with acceptance criteria per above and tag for next planning sprint. ETA to team docs: 3 business days.
ops-bot: Scheduled a follow-up sync: Wednesday 15:00 UTC.
Tyler (CSM): thanks all :thumbsup:
